title: A statement line meets one side of a transfer or a ticked card payment: it attaches to that side, never counted twice (final_review_2 S1, S1b, decision Q1)
story: Set up Mon 4 Jan 2027: the bank holds 300,000, cash and an e-wallet nothing. A card closes on the 15th and is paid on the 10th of the next month (moved later) from the bank; its statement of 15 Dec holds 50,000, not paid yet. On Wed 6 Jan the person takes 10,000 cash from the ATM and types it as a transfer from the bank to cash. On Fri 8 Jan they top up the e-wallet with 1,000 from the bank and type it as a transfer; the money reaches the e-wallet on Mon 11 Jan. On Sat 9 Jan they type the e-wallet app's figure, 0 (nothing has arrived). On Mon 11 Jan the check-in ticks the card payment of 50,000 (it writes the repay set:c@2027-01-10). On Wed 13 Jan the bank statement is read: three plain lines out, the ATM 10,000 on 6 Jan, the top-up 1,000 on 8 Jan and the card company 50,000 on 11 Jan. The same morning the e-wallet statement is read: 1,000 in on Mon 11 Jan. Each line attaches to the side of the record it meets (the bank side sets its posted date and source; the e-wallet side sets `posted2` and `src2`) and is never a second record. Every amount is made up.

events.note: the e-wallet app shows 0: the top-up has not arrived

asks.question: bank_today
asks.why: 300,000 (opening) - 10,000 (ATM transfer to cash, Wed 6 Jan; the statement line attaches to its bank side) - 1,000 (top-up, Fri 8 Jan; the statement line attaches) - 50,000 (card payment ticked Mon 11 Jan; the statement line attaches) = 239,000
asks.note: Before Q1 each statement line was a second spend: 300,000 - 61,000 - 61,000 = 178,000.

asks.question: owed_now
asks.why: 50,000 (statement of 15 Dec) - 50,000 (the ticked payment, its bank side now posted 11 Jan) = 0

asks.question: not_explained
asks.why: 0 (opening) + 0 (the top-up reached the e-wallet Mon 11 Jan, its posted2, after the check) - 0 (check, Sat 9 Jan) = 0
asks.note: The e-wallet statement sets the transfer's second side's posted date (`posted2`), so the current check of Sat 9 Jan does not hold it. Before Q1 the typed top-up was inside the check and the gap of 1,000 was a filler.

asks.question: bank_today
asks.why: 0 (check, Sat 9 Jan) + 1,000 (top-up, posted2 Mon 11 Jan; the e-wallet line attaches to it) = 1,000

asks.question: total
asks.note: 300,000 at the opening less the 50,000 paid to the card: the transfers move money between own accounts, so Total moves only by the card payment.
